name: Organs
note: Major organs. Ids match data-id attributes in assets/svg/organs-anterior.svg and organs-posterior.svg.

structures.name: Brain
structures.location: Inside the cranium, above and behind the eyes.
structures.summary: The control centre of the nervous system: about 1.4 kg of neurons and support cells that process the senses, control movement and generate thought, memory and emotion.
functions: Interprets the senses and controls movement
Regulates breathing, heart rate and hormones through the brainstem and hypothalamus
Memory, language, emotion and reasoning

issues.name: Stroke
issues.note: Sudden face drooping, arm weakness or slurred speech. Call emergency services immediately (think FAST).

issues.name: Migraine
issues.note: A throbbing, often one-sided headache with nausea and sensitivity to light, sometimes after a visual aura.

issues.name: Concussion
issues.note: Headache, confusion or dizziness after a head injury. Vomiting, a worsening headache or drowsiness needs urgent care.

issues.name: Meningitis
issues.note: Fever, severe headache, stiff neck, light sensitivity or a rash that doesn’t fade under a glass. It is an emergency.

structures.name: Pituitary gland
structures.location: At the base of the brain behind the bridge of the nose, sitting in a saddle-shaped hollow of the sphenoid bone (the sella turcica).
structures.summary: A pea-sized gland hanging from the hypothalamus on a thin stalk. Often called the master gland, its hormones drive the thyroid, the adrenal glands, the ovaries and testes, growth and milk production.

members.name: Anterior pituitary
members.note: Makes growth hormone and prolactin, and the hormones that drive the thyroid (TSH), the adrenal glands (ACTH) and the ovaries or testes (FSH and LH).

members.name: Posterior pituitary
members.note: Releases two hormones made in the hypothalamus: antidiuretic hormone (ADH), which controls water balance, and oxytocin, for birth and breastfeeding.

functions: Controls the thyroid, the adrenal glands and the ovaries or testes
Growth hormone drives growth in childhood and tissue repair throughout life
ADH tells the kidneys how much water to keep

issues.name: Pituitary adenoma
issues.note: A usually benign growth. It can cause headaches, loss of side vision, or symptoms from too much or too little of a hormone.

issues.name: Diabetes insipidus
issues.note: Passing large amounts of dilute urine with constant thirst, from too little ADH. It is not related to sugar diabetes.

structures.name: Eye
structures.location: In the orbit, a bony socket in the skull, cushioned by fat and turned by six small muscles.
structures.summary: A fluid-filled ball about 24 mm across. The cornea and lens focus light onto the retina, which turns it into nerve signals that the optic nerve carries to the brain.

members.name: Cornea
members.note: The clear front window, which does most of the focusing.

members.name: Iris and pupil
members.note: The coloured ring, which widens or narrows the pupil to let in more or less light.

members.name: Lens
members.note: Changes shape to focus on near or distant things.

members.name: Retina
members.note: The light-sensitive lining at the back. Its centre, the macula, gives sharp detail and colour.

members.name: Eye muscles
members.note: Six small muscles that turn the eye, worked by the oculomotor, trochlear and abducens nerves.

functions: Focuses light and turns it into nerve signals
Adjusts to bright and dim light
Tears keep the surface clean and moist

issues.name: Conjunctivitis (pink eye)
issues.note: A red, gritty or sticky eye from an infection or allergy. It usually settles by itself.

issues.name: Urgent eye symptoms
issues.note: A painful red eye, sudden loss or blurring of vision, new flashes and floaters, or a shadow spreading over the vision needs urgent same-day care.

issues.name: Cataract
issues.note: Cloudy or dim vision and glare from lights as the lens clouds with age. Treatable with surgery.

issues.name: Glaucoma
issues.note: Raised pressure slowly damages the optic nerve, often without symptoms at first. Regular eye tests catch it.

structures.name: Ear
structures.location: On each side of the head. The outer ear leads through the ear canal to the eardrum; the middle and inner ear lie inside the temporal bone.
structures.summary: The organ of hearing and balance. The outer ear gathers sound, three tiny bones in the middle ear amplify it and the cochlea turns it into nerve signals, while the semicircular canals sense movement of the head.

members.name: Outer ear
members.note: The visible auricle and the ear canal, ending at the eardrum.

members.name: Middle ear
members.note: An air-filled space with the three ossicles (malleus, incus and stapes), joined to the throat by the Eustachian tube.

members.name: Inner ear
members.note: The cochlea for hearing, and the semicircular canals and vestibule for balance.

functions: Hearing
Balance, and sensing movement of the head
The Eustachian tube evens out pressure on the eardrum

issues.name: Middle ear infection (otitis media)
issues.note: Earache, often with a cold and especially in children. It usually settles within a few days.

issues.name: Outer ear infection (otitis externa)
issues.note: An itchy, painful ear canal, often after swimming.

issues.name: Earwax build-up
issues.note: Muffled hearing and a full feeling. Avoid cotton buds; ear drops can soften it.

issues.name: Sudden hearing loss or vertigo
issues.note: Sudden hearing loss in one ear needs same-day assessment. Vertigo with weakness, slurred speech or double vision is an emergency.

structures.name: Skin
structures.listOnly: Not drawn on the map: it covers the whole body, so a drawing of it would hide everything underneath.
structures.location: Covers the whole body, about 1.5–2 m² in an adult. Thickest on the soles and palms, thinnest on the eyelids.
structures.summary: The body’s largest organ, at about 4 kg. It is a waterproof barrier against germs, sun and injury, helps control temperature, and is packed with receptors for touch, pain, heat and cold.

members.name: Epidermis
members.note: The thin outer layer, renewed about every month. It makes melanin, and vitamin D in sunlight.

members.name: Dermis
members.note: The tough inner layer with blood vessels, nerve endings, hair roots and sweat and oil glands.

members.name: Subcutaneous fat
members.note: Insulates, cushions and stores energy.

functions: A barrier against germs, water loss and ultraviolet light
Controls temperature by sweating and changing blood flow
Senses touch, pain, heat and cold
Makes vitamin D in sunlight

issues.name: Eczema
issues.note: Dry, itchy, inflamed patches, often in skin creases. Moisturisers help.

issues.name: Cellulitis
issues.note: Spreading red, hot, swollen and painful skin, often with fever. It needs a doctor promptly.

issues.name: Skin cancer warning signs
issues.note: A mole that changes size, shape or colour, bleeds or itches, or a sore that doesn’t heal needs checking.

issues.name: Shingles
issues.note: A painful band of blistering rash on one side of the body, along one nerve.

structures.name: Pineal gland
structures.location: Deep in the middle of the brain, between its two halves, behind the third ventricle.
structures.summary: A tiny pine-cone-shaped gland that releases melatonin in the dark, helping to set the body’s sleep–wake rhythm.
functions: Releases melatonin at night, which helps bring on sleep
Keeps the body clock in step with day and night

issues.name: Pineal cyst
issues.note: Common, small and usually harmless, often found by chance on a brain scan.

issues.name: Calcification
issues.note: It gathers calcium with age. This shows up on scans and is normal.

structures.name: Thyroid gland
structures.location: Front of the neck, wrapped around the windpipe below the Adam’s apple.
structures.summary: A butterfly-shaped gland whose hormones set the pace of the body’s metabolism.
functions: Produces thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3)
Sets metabolic rate, heart rate and body temperature
Makes calcitonin, which helps regulate calcium

issues.name: Underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism)
issues.note: Tiredness, weight gain, feeling cold, constipation, dry skin.

issues.name: Overactive thyroid (hyperthyroidism)
issues.note: Weight loss, a racing heart, tremor, heat intolerance, anxiety.

issues.name: Goitre or nodule
issues.note: A swelling or lump at the front of the neck that moves when you swallow. Get it checked.

structures.name: Parathyroid glands
structures.location: On the back of the thyroid gland, usually two behind each lobe.
structures.summary: Usually four rice-grain-sized glands that keep the level of calcium in the blood steady with parathyroid hormone (PTH).
functions: Raise blood calcium when it falls, drawing on the bones
Tell the kidneys to keep calcium and to activate vitamin D
Steady calcium keeps nerves and muscles working normally

issues.name: Overactive parathyroid (hyperparathyroidism)
issues.note: Too much calcium: thirst, kidney stones, thinning bones, tummy pain, low mood and tiredness. Often found on a routine blood test.

issues.name: Low calcium after neck surgery
issues.note: Tingling around the mouth or in the fingers, or muscle cramps, after thyroid surgery needs prompt medical advice.

structures.name: Adrenal gland
structures.location: On top of each kidney, high at the back of the abdomen beside the spine (about T12).
structures.summary: A small gland of about 5 g with two layers that work as separate glands: the outer cortex makes steroid hormones and the inner medulla releases adrenaline.

sideNotes.right: The right adrenal is a small pyramid capping the top of the kidney, tucked behind the liver and the inferior vena cava.
sideNotes.left: The left adrenal is a crescent along the upper inner edge of the kidney, behind the stomach and pancreas.

members.name: Adrenal cortex
members.note: Makes cortisol (stress and blood sugar), aldosterone (salt and blood pressure) and small amounts of sex hormones.

members.name: Adrenal medulla
members.note: Releases adrenaline and noradrenaline for the “fight or flight” response.

functions: Cortisol helps the body handle stress, keeps blood sugar up and damps down inflammation
Aldosterone balances salt, water and blood pressure
Adrenaline readies the body for action: a faster heart and more blood to the muscles

issues.name: Adrenal insufficiency (Addison’s disease)
issues.note: Tiredness, weight loss, dizziness on standing, salt craving and darker skin. Vomiting, confusion or collapse is an emergency (adrenal crisis).

issues.name: Cushing’s syndrome
issues.note: Too much cortisol, most often from steroid medicines: weight gain on the trunk and face, thin skin, easy bruising and high blood pressure.

issues.name: Adrenal tumour
issues.note: Usually benign and found by chance on a scan. Rarely one releases bursts of adrenaline, with pounding headaches, sweating and a racing heart.

structures.name: Pharynx
structures.location: Behind the nose, mouth and larynx, from the base of the skull down to the sixth cervical vertebra, where it becomes the oesophagus.
structures.summary: A muscular funnel about 12–14 cm long, shared by air and food. It carries air on to the larynx and, when you swallow, squeezes food down into the oesophagus.

members.name: Nasopharynx
members.note: Behind the nose. Holds the adenoids and the openings of the Eustachian tubes to the middle ears.

members.name: Oropharynx
members.note: Behind the mouth, with the palatine tonsils and the back of the tongue.

members.name: Laryngopharynx
members.note: Behind the larynx, down to the start of the oesophagus.

functions: Carries air from the nose and mouth to the larynx
Swallowing: its muscles push food down while the airway is sealed off
Tonsils and adenoids in its walls guard against infection
Shapes the sound of the voice

issues.name: Sore throat (pharyngitis)
issues.note: Usually viral and better within a week. A severe sore throat with fever, or one side much worse than the other, needs a doctor.

issues.name: Trouble swallowing or breathing
issues.note: Drooling, being unable to swallow saliva, or noisy breathing with a sore throat is an emergency.

issues.name: Lump-in-the-throat feeling (globus)
issues.note: Common and usually harmless when food goes down normally. Get it checked if it lasts, or if swallowing becomes difficult or painful.

structures.name: Nose and nasal cavity
structures.location: The middle of the face, from between the eyes to the nostrils. The nasal cavity behind opens into the nasopharynx.
structures.summary: The entrance to the airway. It warms, moistens and filters the air, and a small patch in its roof holds the smell receptors.

members.name: Nasal septum
members.note: Divides the nose into left and right halves: bone at the back, cartilage at the front.

members.name: Nasal conchae
members.note: Three curled shelves on each side wall that warm and moisten the air.

members.name: Paranasal sinuses
members.note: Air spaces in the frontal, maxillary, ethmoid and sphenoid bones that drain into the nose.

members.name: Olfactory area
members.note: A small patch in the roof of the nasal cavity with the smell receptors.

functions: Warms, moistens and filters the air
Smell
Gives the voice its resonance

issues.name: Sinusitis
issues.note: Facial pain and pressure, a blocked nose and thick discharge after a cold, usually settling within 2–3 weeks.

issues.name: Nosebleed
issues.note: Lean forward and pinch the soft part of the nose for 10–15 minutes. Bleeding for more than 20 minutes, or after a head injury, needs urgent care.

issues.name: Hay fever
issues.note: Sneezing, an itchy runny nose and itchy eyes at certain times of year.

issues.name: Loss of smell
issues.note: Common after colds. If it lasts more than a few weeks, see a doctor.

structures.name: Tongue
structures.location: Floor of the mouth, anchored to the hyoid bone and the jaw. Its back third faces the throat.
structures.summary: A muscular organ that moves food while chewing, starts each swallow, shapes speech and carries most of the taste buds.
functions: Taste: sweet, sour, salty, bitter and umami
Moves food around and pushes it back to swallow
Shapes sounds for speech

issues.name: Mouth ulcers
issues.note: Small painful sores that heal within 2 weeks. An ulcer or patch lasting more than 3 weeks needs checking.

issues.name: Oral thrush
issues.note: White patches that wipe off and leave soreness, common after antibiotics or with steroid inhalers.

issues.name: Swelling of the tongue or lips
issues.note: With difficulty breathing or swallowing, it is an emergency (anaphylaxis).

structures.name: Salivary glands
structures.location: In front of each ear (parotid), under the jaw (submandibular) and under the tongue (sublingual).
structures.summary: Three pairs of major glands, plus hundreds of tiny ones in the lining of the mouth, that make 0.5–1.5 litres of saliva a day.

members.name: Parotid gland
members.note: The largest, in front of the ear over the angle of the jaw. Its duct opens inside the cheek beside the upper second molar.

members.name: Submandibular gland
members.note: Under the jaw. Its duct opens under the tongue.

members.name: Sublingual gland
members.note: The smallest, under the tongue (not drawn).

functions: Saliva moistens food and starts digesting starch
Protects the teeth and fights germs
Helps taste, chewing, swallowing and speech

issues.name: Mumps
issues.note: Painful swelling of the parotid glands with fever. Vaccination prevents it.

issues.name: Salivary stone
issues.note: Pain and swelling under the jaw or in front of the ear at mealtimes.

issues.name: Dry mouth
issues.note: Common with many medicines, dehydration and some conditions.

structures.name: Larynx
structures.location: Front of the neck, between the hyoid bone and the trachea (about C3–C6). The Adam’s apple is the ridge of its thyroid cartilage.
structures.summary: The voice box: a framework of cartilages, muscles and vocal folds that guards the entrance to the airway and makes the sound of the voice.

members.name: Thyroid cartilage
members.note: The shield at the front. Its ridge is the Adam’s apple.

members.name: Cricoid cartilage
members.note: The only complete ring of cartilage in the airway, just below the thyroid cartilage.

members.name: Epiglottis
members.note: A leaf-shaped flap that tips back over the airway when you swallow.

members.name: Vocal folds
members.note: Two bands that vibrate in the outgoing air to make the voice.

functions: Closes the airway when you swallow
Produces the voice
Sets off coughing to clear the airway

issues.name: Laryngitis
issues.note: A hoarse or lost voice after a cold or overuse, usually better within 2 weeks.

issues.name: Hoarseness that lasts
issues.note: Hoarseness for more than 3 weeks, especially in smokers, needs checking by a doctor.

issues.name: Croup
issues.note: A barking cough and noisy breathing in a young child, usually after a cold. Struggling to breathe needs urgent care.

structures.name: Trachea
structures.location: From the front of the neck to the middle of the chest, where it splits into the left and right main bronchi.
structures.summary: The windpipe: a tube about 10–12 cm long, held open by C-shaped rings of cartilage, that carries air from the larynx to the lungs.
functions: Carries air to and from the lungs
Mucus and tiny hairs (cilia) sweep trapped particles upward
Coughing clears and protects the airway

issues.name: Bronchitis
issues.note: A chesty cough and soreness behind the breastbone after a cold.

issues.name: Choking
issues.note: Unable to speak, cough or breathe. Act immediately with back blows and abdominal thrusts, and call emergency services.

issues.name: Inhaled object
issues.note: Small objects usually lodge in the right main bronchus, which is wider and more vertical.

structures.name: Esophagus
structures.location: Behind the trachea and heart, passing through the diaphragm to the stomach.
structures.summary: A muscular tube about 25 cm long that pushes swallowed food down to the stomach in waves (peristalsis).
functions: Moves food and drink to the stomach
A lower sphincter stops stomach acid flowing back up

issues.name: Acid reflux (GERD)
issues.note: Heartburn and an acid taste, worse lying down or after large meals.

issues.name: Difficulty swallowing
issues.note: Food sticking on the way down, especially if it is getting worse or comes with weight loss, needs prompt assessment.

structures.name: Lung
structures.location: Either side of the heart inside the rib cage, from just above the collarbone down to the diaphragm.
structures.summary: Spongy organs where oxygen enters the blood and carbon dioxide leaves, across hundreds of millions of tiny air sacs (alveoli).

sideNotes.right: The right lung has three lobes (upper, middle and lower) and is shorter and wider, because the liver sits below it.
sideNotes.left: The left lung has two lobes (upper and lower) and a notch where the heart sits.

functions: Gas exchange: oxygen in, carbon dioxide out
Helps control the acidity of the blood
Filters small clots out of the circulation

issues.name: Pneumonia
issues.note: Fever, cough with phlegm, breathlessness, and sharp chest pain when breathing in.

issues.name: Asthma / COPD
issues.note: Wheezing, coughing and breathlessness from narrowed airways.

issues.name: Collapsed lung (pneumothorax)
issues.note: Sudden one-sided chest pain and breathlessness. It is urgent.

issues.name: Pulmonary embolism
issues.note: Sudden breathlessness, chest pain or coughing blood, often with a swollen calf. It is an emergency.

structures.name: Heart
structures.location: Middle of the chest behind the sternum, tilted to the left. Its tip (apex) lies near the fifth rib space.
structures.summary: A fist-sized, four-chambered muscular pump. The right side sends blood through the lungs and the left side pumps it around the body, about 100,000 beats a day.
functions: Pumps about 5 litres of blood a minute at rest
Its own electrical system sets the rhythm
Four valves keep blood flowing one way

issues.name: Heart attack
issues.note: Crushing or tight chest pain, possibly spreading to the arm, jaw or back, with sweating or breathlessness. Call emergency services.

issues.name: Angina
issues.note: Chest tightness on exertion that eases with rest. It needs medical assessment.

issues.name: Arrhythmia
issues.note: Palpitations, fluttering, or a racing or irregular pulse. With fainting or chest pain, get urgent care.

issues.name: Heart failure
issues.note: Breathlessness, swollen ankles and tiredness.

structures.name: Liver
structures.location: Upper right abdomen under the right ribs, reaching across the midline.
structures.summary: The largest internal organ (about 1.5 kg). It processes everything absorbed from the gut, makes bile and many proteins, stores energy and clears toxins.
functions: Makes bile to digest fats
Stores glycogen, vitamins and iron
Breaks down drugs and alcohol
Produces clotting factors and albumin

issues.name: Fatty liver disease
issues.note: Often silent, and linked to weight, diabetes and alcohol.

issues.name: Hepatitis
issues.note: Inflammation from viruses, alcohol or drugs: tiredness, yellow skin or eyes (jaundice), dark urine.

issues.name: Cirrhosis
issues.note: Long-term scarring: a swollen belly, easy bruising, confusion.

structures.name: Gallbladder
structures.location: Under the lower edge of the liver, where the right costal margin meets the midclavicular line.
structures.summary: A small pear-shaped pouch that stores and concentrates bile, squeezing it into the duodenum after fatty meals.
functions: Stores and concentrates bile
Releases bile to help digest fats

issues.name: Gallstones (biliary colic)
issues.note: Severe pain under the right ribs or in the upper middle, often after fatty food, lasting minutes to hours. It can spread to the right shoulder blade.

issues.name: Cholecystitis
issues.note: Persistent pain under the right ribs with fever. It needs medical care.

issues.name: Jaundice
issues.note: Yellow skin or eyes with pale stools and dark urine may mean a stone is blocking the bile duct.

structures.name: Stomach
structures.location: Upper left and central abdomen, just under the diaphragm.
structures.summary: A stretchy, J-shaped bag that stores food, churns it and starts protein digestion with acid and enzymes.
functions: Stores and mixes food
Secretes acid and pepsin
Releases food gradually into the small intestine

issues.name: Indigestion / gastritis
issues.note: Burning pain in the upper abdomen, bloating, nausea.

issues.name: Peptic ulcer
issues.note: Gnawing upper-abdominal pain, sometimes eased or worsened by food. Black stools or vomiting blood is an emergency.

issues.name: Gastroenteritis
issues.note: Vomiting and diarrhoea, usually viral. Watch for dehydration.

structures.name: Duodenum
structures.location: Curves in a C around the head of the pancreas, from the stomach (about L1, right of the midline) to just left of the midline, behind the transverse colon.
structures.summary: The first 25 cm or so of the small intestine. It receives food from the stomach and mixes it with bile and pancreatic juice, which enter through a small opening in its wall (the major duodenal papilla).

members.name: Superior part
members.note: Starts at the pylorus. Its first, widened stretch (the duodenal cap) is where most duodenal ulcers form.

members.name: Descending part
members.note: Runs down beside the head of the pancreas. The bile and pancreatic ducts open into it.

members.name: Horizontal part
members.note: Crosses the midline in front of the aorta and the inferior vena cava.

members.name: Ascending part
members.note: Rises to the duodenojejunal flexure, where the jejunum begins.

functions: Receives bile and pancreatic enzymes
Neutralises stomach acid with bicarbonate
Releases hormones (secretin and cholecystokinin) that pace digestion
Absorbs iron

issues.name: Duodenal ulcer
issues.note: A burning or gnawing pain in the upper middle abdomen, often eased by eating and worse at night. Black stools or vomiting blood is an emergency.

issues.name: Coeliac disease
issues.note: Gluten damages the lining here first, so a small sample (biopsy) from the duodenum confirms it.

structures.name: Spleen
structures.location: Upper left abdomen behind the stomach, sheltered by ribs 9–11.
structures.summary: A fist-sized organ that filters the blood, removes old red cells and stores immune cells that fight infection.
functions: Filters blood and recycles old red blood cells
Immune defence against bacteria
Stores platelets and white cells

issues.name: Ruptured spleen
issues.note: After a blow to the left side: left upper pain, sometimes pain at the tip of the left shoulder, and dizziness. It is an emergency.

issues.name: Enlarged spleen
issues.note: From infections such as glandular fever (avoid contact sports while it is enlarged), or from liver or blood conditions.

structures.name: Pancreas
structures.location: Deep in the upper abdomen behind the stomach, its head tucked into the curve of the duodenum.
structures.summary: A long gland with two jobs: it releases digestive enzymes into the gut, and hormones (insulin and glucagon) into the blood.

members.name: Head
members.note: Tucked into the curve of the duodenum.

members.name: Body
members.note: Crosses the spine behind the stomach.

members.name: Tail
members.note: Reaches the spleen.

members.name: Pancreatic islets
members.note: About a million clusters of hormone cells (islets of Langerhans), only 1–2% of the gland, that release insulin and glucagon into the blood.

functions: Digestive enzymes for fats, proteins and carbohydrates
Insulin and glucagon control blood sugar
Bicarbonate neutralises stomach acid

issues.name: Pancreatitis
issues.note: Severe upper-abdominal pain boring through to the back, with vomiting. Often from gallstones or alcohol, and urgent.

issues.name: Diabetes
issues.note: Thirst, passing a lot of urine, weight loss and tiredness.

issues.name: Pancreatic cancer
issues.note: Painless jaundice, back pain and weight loss. See a doctor promptly.

structures.name: Kidney
structures.location: High at the back of the abdomen either side of the spine (about T12–L3), partly behind the lowest ribs. The right one sits a little lower.
structures.summary: Bean-shaped filters that process about 180 litres of blood plasma a day into 1–2 litres of urine, balancing water, salts and blood pressure.
functions: Filters waste from the blood into urine
Balances fluids, salts and acidity
Makes hormones for blood pressure (renin) and red-cell production (EPO)
Activates vitamin D

issues.name: Kidney stone
issues.note: Waves of severe pain in the flank spreading to the groin, sometimes with blood in the urine.

issues.name: Kidney infection (pyelonephritis)
issues.note: Flank pain, fever, shivering and urinary symptoms. See a doctor the same day.

issues.name: Chronic kidney disease
issues.note: Usually silent, and found with blood and urine tests. Worth checking with diabetes or high blood pressure.

structures.name: Ureter
structures.location: From each kidney down the back wall of the abdomen, over the brim of the pelvis, to the back of the bladder.
structures.summary: A muscular tube about 25–30 cm long that carries urine from the kidney to the bladder in waves (peristalsis).
functions: Carries urine from the kidney to the bladder
Squeezes it along in waves, several times a minute
Enters the bladder at a slant, which stops urine flowing back up

issues.name: Kidney stone in the ureter (renal colic)
issues.note: Waves of severe pain from the flank to the groin as a stone moves down, often with nausea. With fever or shivering, get urgent care.

issues.name: Blockage
issues.note: A stone or a narrowing can back urine up and swell the kidney (hydronephrosis), which a scan shows.

structures.name: Small intestine
structures.location: Coiled in the centre of the abdomen, framed by the large intestine.
structures.summary: About 6 metres of coiled tube where most digestion and nutrient absorption happen, across millions of finger-like villi. It runs from the duodenum (shown separately) through the jejunum to the ileum.
functions: Digests food with enzymes and bile
Absorbs nutrients, water and vitamins
Hosts a large part of the immune system

issues.name: Coeliac disease
issues.note: Gluten triggers inflammation: bloating, diarrhoea, weight loss, anaemia.

issues.name: Bowel obstruction
issues.note: Colicky pain, a swollen belly, vomiting and no wind or stools. It is an emergency.

issues.name: Crohn’s disease
issues.note: Inflammation causing pain, diarrhoea and weight loss, often at the end of the ileum in the lower right.

structures.name: Large intestine
structures.location: Frames the abdomen: up the right side, across under the stomach, then down the left side into the pelvis, where it becomes the rectum.
structures.summary: About 1.5 m long (caecum and colon), ending in the rectum. It absorbs water and salts, hosts trillions of gut bacteria and forms stool.
functions: Absorbs water and salts
Gut bacteria ferment fibre and make vitamins
Forms stool and moves it on to the rectum

issues.name: Constipation / IBS
issues.note: Cramping, bloating and a change in bowel habit. Very common.

issues.name: Diverticulitis
issues.note: Pain in the lower left abdomen with fever, mostly in older adults.

issues.name: Bowel cancer warning signs
issues.note: Blood in the stool, a lasting change in bowel habit, unexplained weight loss or anaemia. See a doctor.

structures.name: Appendix
structures.location: Lower right abdomen, hanging from the caecum.
structures.summary: A finger-sized pouch off the start of the large intestine. It holds lymphoid tissue and may act as a reservoir for helpful gut bacteria.
functions: Lymphoid (immune) tissue
A possible reservoir of gut bacteria

issues.name: Appendicitis
issues.note: Pain that starts around the navel and moves to the lower right, worse with movement or coughing, with loss of appetite, nausea and fever. It is urgent.

structures.name: Rectum
structures.location: At the back of the pelvis, following the curve of the sacrum and coccyx, from the end of the sigmoid colon (about S3) down to the anus.
structures.summary: The last 12 cm or so of the large intestine. It holds stool until it is convenient to pass, and stretch sensors in its wall create the urge to go.

members.name: Rectal ampulla
members.note: The wide lower part where stool waits.

members.name: Anal canal
members.note: The last 3–4 cm, ringed by the internal (automatic) and external (voluntary) anal sphincters.

functions: Holds stool until you pass it
Senses fullness and triggers the urge to go
The sphincters and pelvic floor keep it closed

issues.name: Piles (haemorrhoids)
issues.note: Bright red blood on the paper, itching or a soft lump at the anus. Common, and usually manageable at home.

issues.name: Anal fissure
issues.note: Sharp pain while passing stool, then a burning ache, with a little bright red blood.

issues.name: Rectal bleeding warning signs
issues.note: Dark or mixed-in blood, a lasting change in bowel habit or weight loss needs a doctor. Heavy bleeding needs urgent care.

structures.name: Urinary bladder
structures.location: Low in the pelvis, behind the pubic bones.
structures.summary: A muscular, stretchy reservoir that holds urine from the kidneys (around 400–500 ml) until it is convenient to empty.
functions: Stores urine
Empties under control of sphincters and the pelvic floor

issues.name: Urinary tract infection (cystitis)
issues.note: Burning, urgency, passing urine often, and low central pain.

issues.name: Urinary retention
issues.note: Unable to pass urine, with a painful, full lower belly. It is urgent.

issues.name: Incontinence
issues.note: Leaking when coughing (stress) or with a sudden urge. Common and treatable.
